images.title: A square, a rectangle and a pentagon
images.purpose: Show the example of the concept: which of three shapes have all their sides equal and so are regular shapes.
images.composition: Three shapes in a row with every side length written next to its side, the shape names above and Regular or Not regular below each.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816, scale 46 px for every 1 cm. THREE SHAPES in a row, all with thin dark #2B2B2B outlines (4 px). (1) A SQUARE filled teal #0072B2, 276 by 276 px (6 cm by 6 cm), x 170 to 446, y 262 to 538. (2) A RECTANGLE filled amber #E69F00, 276 wide by 184 high (6 cm by 4 cm), x 590 to 866, y 308 to 492. (3) A REGULAR PENTAGON filled teal #0072B2 with every side 138 px (3 cm) and one corner pointing up, its 5 corners at (x, y) = (1228, 283), (1116, 364), (1159, 495), (1297, 495), (1340, 364), the centre at (1228, 400). SIDE LENGTH LABELS, 30 px dark #1F2937, one on every side, centred outside the side: the square has the text 6 cm on all 4 sides (centred at (308, 236) above, (308, 578) below, (114, 410) left, (502, 410) right); the rectangle has 6 cm on its top and bottom sides (centred at (728, 282) and (728, 532)) and 4 cm on its left and right sides (centred at (534, 410) and (922, 410)); the pentagon has 3 cm on all 5 sides, centred outside each side at (x, y) = (1150, 292), (1102, 441), (1228, 533), (1354, 441), (1306, 292). So there are 13 length labels in all: eleven of them are 6 cm or 3 cm and two are 4 cm. SHAPE NAMES above the shapes, bold 40 px dark #1F2937, centred at y 150: Square at x 308, Rectangle at x 728, Pentagon at x 1228. CAPTIONS below the shapes, 40 px, centred at y 660: Regular under the square (x 308), Not regular under the rectangle (x 728), Regular under the pentagon (x 1228). Nothing else in the frame, no tick marks, no angle marks.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of shapes or side labels that differs from the numbers stated in the spec, or a side label with a wrong length
a pentagon with unequal sides, a rectangle drawn as a square, or any angle mark, tick mark or number beyond the listed labels
images.takeaway: A shape whose sides are all equal is a regular shape: the square and the pentagon are, the rectangle is not.
images.description: A square with every side 6 cm, a rectangle 6 cm by 4 cm and a pentagon with every side 3 cm, labelled Regular, Not regular and Regular.
images.context: Concept image for Regular Shapes. It follows the idea of the figures in your maths book (a regular pentagon with equal sides, and shapes with equal sides called regular shapes) and uses the concept's own sizes.
images.teaching_notes: Read the side labels with the child and ask whether all of them are the same. The slip to watch: calling a rectangle regular because its opposite sides match.

image_decisions.why: The three shapes with their side lengths show which shapes have all sides equal and so are regular shapes.
